source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Economics Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. What is Work
points: **Work** = any activity done to **produce goods or services**, meet needs, or **earn a living**.
Everyone works — at home, on farms, in offices, shops and factories.
Work turns human **effort and skill** into things and services that people need.

sections.heading: 2. Dignity of Labour
points: **Every kind of work has value and dignity** — no work is 'high' or 'low'.
A farmer, a teacher, a cleaner, a doctor and a carpenter all contribute to society.
Respecting all workers is called the **dignity of labour** — a key value.
We are **interdependent**: each person's work depends on the work of many others.

sections.heading: 3. Types of Work

sub: **Paid work** — done for wages/income (e.g. a shopkeeper, a driver).
**Unpaid work** — done without direct payment but very valuable (e.g. **household work, caring for family, farming for the home**).
**Physical (manual) work** — mainly bodily effort (e.g. a mason).
**Mental work** — mainly thinking/knowledge (e.g. a teacher, an engineer).

points: Most jobs mix **both** physical and mental effort.

sections.heading: 4. Work and Livelihood
points: **Livelihood** = the means by which a person earns a living.
Work gives **income, self-respect and a place in society**.
Unpaid work (like housework) is often unrecognised, though it is essential.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Work = activity to produce goods/services or earn a living.
Dignity of labour = all work has value; no job is high or low.
Paid work = for income; unpaid work = e.g. household/care work (valuable but unpaid).
Physical work = bodily effort; mental work = thinking/knowledge.
Livelihood = means of earning a living; we are interdependent.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Unpaid work is still valuable** — household and care work are real work, just not paid.
'Dignity of labour' means **all** work deserves respect, manual and mental alike.
Livelihood = **how** one earns a living (not the same as merely 'a job title').
